notes: Post-27th Constitutional Amendment (Nov 2025) hierarchy and appellate routing.

courts.name: Federal Constitutional Court of Pakistan
courts.lawyer_review_flag: needs lawyer review: 27th Amendment relative apex rank between FCC and SC, jurisdiction delineation, and bench composition. Source: 27th Amendment Act (Nov 2025).
courts.source: Constitution of Pakistan, 27th Amendment Act (Nov 2025), Art. 175A / Part VII
courts.span_pointer: 27th Amendment Act 2025, establishing Federal Constitutional Court as apex constitutional court
courts.jurisdiction: Apex constitutional court; exclusive jurisdiction over constitutional disputes between governments, constitutional interpretation, and challenges to constitutional amendments.

courts.name: Supreme Court of Pakistan
courts.lawyer_review_flag: needs lawyer review: FCC/Supreme Court equal-rank entry and jurisdictional boundaries post-27th Amendment. Source: Constitution of Pakistan 1973, Arts. 175A, 184, 185.
courts.span_pointer: Constitution of Pakistan 1973, Chapter 2, Part VII (Arts. 176-191)
courts.jurisdiction: Apex appellate court for general, civil, criminal, and commercial matters.

courts.name: Supreme Court Shariat Appellate Bench
courts.source: Constitution of Pakistan 1973, Art. 203F, Art. 203D(2) proviso
courts.span_pointer: Art. 203F & Art. 203D(2) proviso: An appeal lies to the Supreme Court from any decision of the Federal Shariat Court. Pendency of appeal suspends FSC declaration of repugnance.
courts.jurisdiction: Appeals against decisions and repugnancy declarations of the Federal Shariat Court.

courts.name: Federal Shariat Court
courts.span_pointer: Art. 203D: Court may examine whether any law is repugnant to Islamic Injunctions. Proviso to 203D(2): Decision takes effect only after appeal period expires or appeal is disposed of.
courts.jurisdiction: Examines whether laws conform to the injunctions of Islam; Hudood revisional and appellate jurisdiction.

courts.name: High Courts (Lahore, Sindh, Peshawar, Balochistan, Islamabad)
courts.source: Constitution of Pakistan 1973, Arts. 192-203; CPC s.96, s.100, s.115; FIO 2001 s.22
courts.span_pointer: Constitution Art. 199 (Writ jurisdiction); FIO 2001 s.22 (Banking Appeals)
courts.jurisdiction: Provincial constitutional writs (Art. 199), first appeals, second appeals, civil and criminal revisions.

courts.name: Banking Court
courts.source: Financial Institutions (Recovery of Finances) Ordinance 2001, Sections 5, 9, 10, 19, 22
courts.span_pointer: Section 22 FIO 2001: Aggrieved party may prefer appeal to High Court. Bar on appeals to District Judge or under s.109 CPC.
courts.jurisdiction: Exclusive civil and criminal jurisdiction over financial institution recovery suits and execution of mortgage decrees.

courts.name: Service Tribunals (Federal Service Tribunal / Provincial Service Tribunals)
courts.source: Constitution of Pakistan 1973, Art. 212; Service Tribunals Act 1973, Section 4
courts.span_pointer: Art. 212(2): Exclusive jurisdiction over civil servant terms and conditions. Civil court suits and Art. 199 writ petitions are barred.
courts.jurisdiction: Exclusive jurisdiction over terms and conditions of civil servants.
courts.appeal_route_to: Supreme Court of Pakistan (Art. 212(3) Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal)
